The Word of Wisdom was first given as a revelation in 1833, but interpretations differ on when it became mandatory. Some sources state that in 1851 Brigham Young proposed a formal covenant to keep the Word of Wisdom and it was unanimously accepted, making it binding as a commandment thereafter [d1,d5,d7]. Other sources indicate that temple recommend requirements—one concrete enforcement mechanism—were not imposed until 1919 (First Presidency letter) or 1921, framing a later threshold for practical mandatory observance [d6,d8,d9]. Because the term “mandatory” can refer either to a binding covenant in 1851 or to enforceable temple worthiness policies in the 1910s–1920s, the evidence presents two defensible dates.
